name: asm6809
desc: Cross assembler targeting the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309
why: A cross assembler for the 6809 and 6309, a door into the rarely visited world of Motorola retro CPUs.

brief.what_it_is: asm6809 is a portable cross assembler for the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309 CPUs, so you write 6809 or 6309 assembly source on a modern machine and it produces machine code for those chips. It accepts arbitrarily complex expressions with most C-style operators, forward references, macros and conditional assembly. Output formats are raw binary, DragonDOS binary, CoCo RS-DOS (DECB) binary, Motorola SREC and Intel HEX. The homepage shows no command-line examples.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation. It presents the tool as a portable assembler for the 6809 and 6309, with the Dragon and Tandy CoCo platforms implied by the DragonDOS and RS-DOS output formats.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the homepage lists a source tarball (asm6809-2.17.tar.gz), a git clone from https://www.6809.org.uk/git/asm6809.git, Debian snapshot builds from an Apt repository, Ubuntu snapshot builds from a Launchpad PPA, and Windows binaries for 64-bit and 32-bit (cross-built with MinGW). No runtime, account or hardware requirement is mentioned. XRoar, a Dragon/CoCo emulator, is named as a way to run the output.
brief.standout: It is a modern, portable cross assembler for a niche CPU family that covers many retro output formats, including the Dragon and CoCo disk and tape formats, so its output can run directly on period-accurate emulators like XRoar. The project also keeps packaged builds for Debian, Ubuntu and Windows.
brief.status: maintained. The current version is 2.17, released 2025-06-15, the homepage was last updated 15 Jun 2025, and the release notes describe a fix to '*' as the current PC in expressions.
brief.caveats: The homepage does not mention a warning or known limitations. Windows binaries are cross-built with MinGW rather than built natively. Licensing is GNU GPL version 3 or later, which matters if you plan to redistribute or embed it. The scout note calls the 6309 'rarely visited', and this is a 6809/6309 cross assembler only, not a general-purpose one.
quotes: asm6809 is a portable cross assembler targeting the Motorola 6809 and Hitachi 6309.
Features arbitrarily complex expressions (with most C-style operators available), forward references, macro expansion and conditional assembly.
